title: Early life exposure to house dust mite allergen prevents experimental allergic asthma requiring mitochondrial H(2)O(2).
ehr_evidence: This is an in vivo/in vitro animal immunology study using transgenic and wild-type mice (MCAT, WT, and OT-II TCR transgenic mice) at the University of Pittsburgh; no electronic health records were used.
summary: A murine experimental model showed that early-life low-dose house dust mite (HDM) exposure establishes stable airway tolerance that requires mitochondrial H2O2 to constrain lung dendritic cell and macrophage numbers and suppress Th2/Th17 responses.
key_findings: Early-life low-dose HDM (0.5 µg) at 2 weeks of age prevented airway inflammation and mucus production upon later challenge, whereas high-dose HDM (5 µg) failed to induce tolerance and instead increased airway inflammation (P<0.05).

Depletion of mitochondrial H2O2 in MCAT mice abolished tolerance, producing eosinophil-rich inflammation, elevated serum IgE, and airway hyperreactivity comparable to inflammation-inducing conditions.
Low-dose HDM significantly reduced IL-13- and IL-5-producing CD4+ T cells versus the No HDM group (P<0.05).
WT tolerized mice showed a 50% decrease in total lung DC numbers versus naïve mice, whereas MCAT tolerized mice harbored ~3x more total DCs, cDC1s, and cDC2s (P<0.05).
RT-qPCR revealed 2x more S100a4:Irf8 and 1.5x more Irf4:Irf8 expression in tolerized MCAT DCs versus tolerized WT DCs.
Lung macrophage numbers showed a trend toward reduction in WT tolerized mice but not MCAT mice.
captured_features: BAL fluid differential cell counts (eosinophils, neutrophils, lymphocytes)
Lung histology inflammation and mucus scores (PAS staining)
Lung mRNA expression (Ifng, Il13, Il17a, Irf4, Irf8, S100a4, Hprt1)
Dendritic cell and macrophage cell numbers
study_design: experimental animal model (in vivo tolerization model with in vitro DC-T cell co-culture)
population: Newborn/2-week old mouse pups and 6-week old mice; wild-type, mitochondrial catalase-overexpressing (MCAT) transgenic, and OT-II TCR transgenic mice
limitations: No HDM-specific TCR transgenic mice were available, so OT-II T cells were used as a surrogate to assess DC function ex vivo.
Infant mice (2-week old) were used, which may differ immunologically from older animals.
LPS contamination of HDM was controlled but residual confounding could not be fully excluded.
